facts.statement: Emiliasaura is an extinct genus of ornithopod dinosaurs from the Early Cretaceous of Argentina.
facts.quote: Emiliasaura (meaning "Emilia's lizard") is an extinct genus of iguanodontian ornithopod dinosaurs from the Early Cretaceous (Valanginian) Mulichinco Formation of Neuquén Province, Argentina.

facts.statement: The genus Emiliasaura contains only one known species, Emiliasaura alessandrii.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Emiliasaura alessandrii, known from three individual specimens.

facts.statement: The fossils were discovered by Carlos Alessandri in the summer of 2009 near Las Lajas, Argentina.
facts.quote: During the summer of 2009, Carlos Alessandri discovered productive outcrops of the Mulichinco Formation (Paraje Pilmatué locality) 9 km northeast of the city of Las Lajas in Neuquén Province, Argentina.

facts.statement: Emiliasaura alessandrii was formally described as a new genus and species in 2025 by Coria and colleagues.
facts.quote: After being announced in October 2024 in a non-finalized preprint, Coria et al. (2025) described Emiliasaura alessandrii as a new genus and species of ornithopod based on these fossil remains.

facts.statement: The genus name honors Emilia Ondettia de Fix, who founded the first museum in Las Lajas.
facts.quote: The generic name, Emiliasaura, honors Emilia Ondettia de Fix, the founder of the first museum in Las Lajas.

facts.statement: The species name honors Carlos Alessandri, the discoverer of the holotype specimen.
facts.quote: The specific name, honors Carlos Alessandri, discoverer of the holotype.

facts.statement: Research indicates that the known specimens of Emiliasaura belonged to subadult individuals that were still growing.
facts.quote: Based on histological research, Coria et al. (2025) identified the specimens of Emiliasaura as belonging to somatically immature, or subadult, individuals.

facts.statement: Emiliasaura lived during the Valanginian age of the Early Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Emiliasaura is known from the Mulichinco Formation, which dates to the Valanginian age of the early Cretaceous period.

facts.statement: Emiliasaura lived approximately 139 to 132 million years ago in what is now South America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 139 a 132 millones de años, durante el Valanginiense, en lo que es hoy Sudamérica.

facts.statement: The fossil record for Emiliasaura spans from 137.05 to 132.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Valanginian to Valanginian (137.05 to 132.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: The environment where Emiliasaura lived included tree ferns and podocarp conifer trees.
facts.quote: Plants known from the formation include the tree fern Tempskya and podocarp conifer trees.

facts.statement: Emiliasaura was initially identified as a rhabdodontomorph, which would make it the oldest known member of that clade.
facts.quote: Emiliasaura was initially described as a rhabdodontomorph. If this identification is correct, it would represent the oldest member of this clade and the first named from South America.

facts.statement: Later analyses placed Emiliasaura outside the Rhabdodontomorpha clade, instead classifying it as a styracosternan.
facts.quote: However, a later analysis of rhabdodontomorphs failed to recover Emiliasaura within this clade, instead placing it as a styracosternan.

facts.statement: One phylogenetic analysis recovered Emiliasaura as the most basal member of the Rhabdodontomorpha.
facts.quote: They found it to be the most basal member of the Rhabdodontomorpha. This would makes it the oldest known member of the clade and the first one known from South America.

facts.statement: Another study concluded that Emiliasaura likely belongs to a genus outside the Rhabdodontomorpha.
facts.quote: The authors concluded that, while they had not observed the material in detail, Emiliasaura can most likely be regarded as a genus outside Rhabdodontomorpha.

facts.statement: A phylogenetic analysis identified Emiliasaura as the most basal member of the Rhabdodontomorpha.
facts.quote: Se introdujo a Emiliasaura en un análisis filogenético y se descubrió que era el miembro más basal de Rhabdodontomorpha.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Emiliasaura is a basal rhabdodontomorph or an early-diverging styracosternan within Dryomorpha.
facts.quote: In a later 2025 publication focused on European rhabdodontomorphs, Czepiński & Madzia included Emiliasaura in an updated version of the comprehensive phylogenetic dataset of Fonseca et al. (2024). This matrix consistently recovered Emiliasaura within Dryomorpha, as an early-diverging styracosternan.

rejected.statement: The first specimen collected in March 2009 included a partial skeleton with a complete right hindlimb and parts of the shoulder.
rejected.quote: The partial skeleton of a medium-sized ornithopod was collected in March of that year, comprising part of the left scapula and coracoid, the left humerus, and a complete right hindlimb.
